$comment: Generated from archive.yaml by `npm run generate` in core. Do not edit.
title: Archive object
description: Metadata of one archive object (an image, a document, ...). One YAML file per object. Files (scans, videos, OCR text, ...) live in the object store and are described in YAML files.

id.description: ULID. Stable and meaningless: never derived from file names or call numbers.

parents.description: The groups (album, collection, ...) this object belongs to; an object can be in several. Only this side is written: the group does not list its members. A group can be in groups too, but not in itself, not through others (checked in CI, not expressible here).

type.description: Object type. Decides which further fields and which files are allowed.

subtype.description: Optional refinement of the type, e.g. photo or letter. The values are listed in archive.yaml.

location.description: The place the object relates to for the archive, as free text: where a photo was taken, where something shown stands. This is the place on the map.

origin.description: Who made the object and where: the photographer and the place of a photo, the sender and the place of a letter, the company and its seat on a brochure. Not where it was found.

original.description: Where the original is, if there is one (there is only one): who has it now, and under which call number.

owner.description: Who the original belongs to, e.g. when that differs from the holder (loan, deposit).

subjects.description: The things the object shows or mentions: people, places, buildings, businesses, events, things.

notes.description: Internal notes of the person capturing the object.

storage.description: Where the content of the object lives: 'local' (default, in our object store, described by files) or 'external' (somewhere else, described by external).

external.description: Where the content is, if it is not here (storage: external). One entry per place.

group.description: A group of objects (an album, a collection, ...). It is described like any object (title, date, origin, original, ...) but has no files and no storage of its own.

stored_here.description: The content lives in our object store (storage: local, the default): the files are the object.

stored_elsewhere.description: The content lives somewhere else (storage: external). Files are optional and only accompany it, e.g. a thumbnail or a screenshot of the page; they are not the object.

image_files.description: Exactly one file with the role 'main'.

document_files.description: One or more pages. 'num' gives the order and must be unique (checked in CI, not expressible here).

external_entry.description: One place outside of our store where the content can be found. Everything is optional (the address may not be known yet), but an entry says at least something.

type.description: What kind of place it is, e.g. archive or platform. The values are listed in archive.yaml.

site.description: Name of the archive or platform, e.g. Arcinsys, YouTube.

uri.description: Link to the object or to its catalogue entry.

reference.description: Call number or id at that place.

note.description: Free text about this place, e.g. where in it to look.

retrieved.description: The day somebody last saw the content there (YYYY-MM-DD).

original.description: The one place where the original is kept. Everything is optional, but an entry says at least something.

holder.description: Who has the original now and where: the town archive, a family, a collector, a gallery. Possession, not ownership.

uri.description: Link to the holder's catalogue entry.

note.description: Free text, e.g. shelf or box.

entity.description: A person, place, building, business, event or thing. The values of type are listed in archive.yaml.

source.description: Where the point comes from, e.g. osm (OpenStreetMap).

file.description: An original file in the object store, e.g. a scan.

role.description: Role of the file within the object (restricted per type).

original_name.description: The name the file had when it was captured (e.g. the scanner's or camera's file name), kept to trace it back.

path.description: Path in the object store, relative to the store root: files/<sha[0,2]>/<sha[2,2]>/<sha>/original.<ext>. Must match sha256 (checked by checkConsistency).

captured_at.description: Capture time from the file's own metadata (EXIF), if present. Not the date of the depicted event.

variants.description: Derived files: previews, other sizes, OCR text, transcripts, key frames.

path.description: Path in the object store: in the directory of the original, <name>.<first 12 hex of the variant sha256>.<ext>, e.g. preview-400.41ab9c03d2e1.jpg. Checked by checkConsistency.

at_seconds.description: For key frames: position in the video.

generator.description: What produced the variant. Use name 'human' for hand-made or hand-corrected variants.

date.description: EDTF date: 1963, 1963-07, 1963-07-14, 196X, 1963?, 1963~, or an interval like 1960/1969. Validated by form only.
